chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Salih ibn Uqbah, from Abdullah ibn Hilal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what is the minimum (reward) for the visitor of the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He said to me, 'O Abdullah! Verily, the minimum that befalls him is that Allah protects him in his own self and his family until He returns him to his family. And when the Day of Resurrection comes, Allah will be the Protector for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum reward for visiting the grave of Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates a tiered reward structure, where the baseline blessing is divine preservation of the visitor and their household during their journey and return. This earthly safeguarding serves as a precursor to the eschatological guarantee, where Allah Himself becomes the ultimate Guardian (Al-Hafiz) on the Day of Judgment, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the intercessory and protective power of the Ahl al-Bayt's shrines. This hadith underscores the continuity between temporal well-being and eternal salvation in the theology of Ziyarah.
